blocks.prompt: 5 To do a piece of work, Abdullah takes 10 days more than Abdul Hadi. Together they finish the work in 12 days. How long would Abdul Hadi take to finish it alone?
blocks.explanation:
A time-and-work word problem: a person who takes \(n\) days does \(\frac{1}{n}\) of the work in one day.
We must find Abdul Hadi's time alone.
Plan: let Abdul Hadi take \(x\) days, add the two one-day works, set equal to \(\frac{1}{12}\), solve.
steps:
Given: Abdullah takes 10 days more than Abdul Hadi; together they take 12 days.
To find: Abdul Hadi's time alone.
Method: Work done in one day \(= \frac{1}{\text{days needed}}\). Working together, the one-day works add up to the one-day work of the pair.

Choose the unknown
\[\text{Abdul Hadi: } x \text{ days}\]
\[\text{Abdullah: } x + 10 \text{ days}\]
Why: Abdullah takes 10 days more.

Form the equation
\[\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x + 10} = \dfrac{1}{12}\]
Why: In one day Abdul Hadi does \(\frac{1}{x}\) of the work, Abdullah \(\frac{1}{x + 10}\), and together \(\frac{1}{12}\).

Clear the fractions
\[12(x + 10) + 12x = x(x + 10)\]
\[24x + 120 = x^2 + 10x\]
Why: Multiply every term by the LCD \(12x(x + 10)\).

Standard form and factorize
\[x^2 - 14x - 120 = 0\]
\[(x - 20)(x + 6) = 0\]
\[x = 20 \text{ or } x = -6\]
Why: \(-20 \times 6 = -120\) and \(-20 + 6 = -14\). Days cannot be negative, so \(x = 20\).

Check
\[\dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{3}{60} + \dfrac{2}{60}\]
\[= \dfrac{5}{60} = \dfrac{1}{12} \;\checkmark\]
Why: Abdullah takes \(20 + 10 = 30\) days; together they finish \(\frac{1}{12}\) of the work per day, i.e. the whole work in 12 days.
blocks.final_answer: Abdul Hadi alone would take 20 days (Abdullah 30 days).
